title: India Eyes Bigger Africa Aid Push Ahead of Summit
excerpt: With IAFS-IV opening in New Delhi on May 31, India signals a transformational leap in its $10B+ development partnership with Africa.
body:
India is preparing to unveil an ambitious new development roadmap for Africa at the fourth India-Africa Forum Summit (IAFS-IV), set to open in New Delhi on May 31, 2026 — the first such gathering in over a decade and the highest-stakes diplomatic event between the two sides since 2015.

**What India Is Bringing to the Table:**
New Delhi already carries significant weight as a development partner: it has extended more than 190 Lines of Credit totalling over $10 billion to 41 African countries, supporting power grids, water systems, digital infrastructure, and transport networks. Officials say IAFS-IV aims to 'impart transformational changes in the relationship,' with cooperation expanding into climate action, critical minerals, space technology, and pharmaceuticals. India's 2025 development grant budget alone earmarked $800 million globally, with a notable increase in Africa's allocation.

**Why This Moment Is Different:**
Africa arrives at this summit facing an aid vacuum. Western donors — including the US, UK, and Germany — have cut development assistance sharply in 2025, creating an opening that India is deliberately stepping into. The African Development Bank and India announced stepped-up cooperation in digital infrastructure just weeks before the summit, with India having contributed $2 million to the African Digital Financial Inclusion Facility and signed a $6 million India Trust Fund agreement with the Bank in 2024. Bilateral India-Africa trade crossed $100 billion in 2024-25, and Indian companies secured $760 million in African Development Bank-financed contracts between 2020 and 2025.

**What to Watch:**
All eyes now turn to May 31, when a joint declaration is expected to outline fresh financial commitments, a renewed Lines of Credit framework, and a concrete agenda aligning India's Viksit Bharat 2047 goals with Africa's Agenda 2063 blueprint.
